\[
xyz = 3,
\]
\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x) = 4,
\]

\]

Let

\[
u=\frac{x-y}{x+y},\qquad v=\frac{y-z}{y+z},\qquad w=\frac{z-x}{z+x}.
\]

Since \(x,y,z>0\), we have \(u,v,w\in(-1,1)\). From the given equations,

\[
uvw=\frac{(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)}{(x+y)(y+z)(z+x)}=\frac{4}{40}=\frac{1}{10}.
\]

Also,

\[
\frac{1-u}{1+u}=\frac{y}{x},\qquad 
\frac{1-v}{1+v}=\frac{z}{y},\qquad 
\frac{1-w}{1+w}=\frac{x}{z}.
\]

Multiplying these three identities gives

\[
(1-u)(1-v)(1-w)=(1+u)(1+v)(1+w),
\]

which simplifies to

\[
u+v+w+uvw=0.
\]

Hence

\[
u+v+w=-\frac{1}{10}.
\]

Now,

\[
\frac{(x+y)(y+z)(z+x)}{xyz}=\frac{40}{3}.
\]

But

\[
\frac{x+y}{x}=\frac{2}{1+u},\qquad
\frac{y+z}{y}=\frac{2}{1+v},\qquad
\frac{z+x}{z}=\frac{2}{1+w},
\]

so

\[
\frac{8}{(1+u)(1+v)(1+w)}=\frac{40}{3}.
\]

Thus

\[
(1+u)(1+v)(1+w)=\frac35.
\]

Expanding and using \(u+v+w+uvw=0\),

\[
1+(uv+vw+wu)=\frac35,
\]

so

\[
uv+vw+wu=-\frac25.
\]

Therefore \(u,v,w\) are the roots of

\[
t^3+\frac{1}{10}t^2-\frac25t-\frac{1}{10}=0,
\]

or

\[
10t^3+t^2-4t-1=0.
\]

Factoring,

\[
10t^3+t^2-4t-1=(2t+1)(5t^2-2t-1),
\]

so

\[
\{u,v,w\}=\left\{-\frac12,\frac{1+\sqrt6}{5},\frac{1-\sqrt6}{5}\right\}.
\]

Now define

\[
R(t)=\frac{1-t}{1+t}.
\]

Then

\[
\frac{y}{x}=R(u),\qquad \frac{z}{y}=R(v).
\]

For the three possible values of \(t\),

\[
R\left(-\frac12\right)=3,
\]

\[
R\left(\frac{1+\sqrt6}{5}\right)
=\frac{4-\sqrt6}{6+\sqrt6}
=\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3},
\]

\[
R\left(\frac{1-\sqrt6}{5}\right)
=\frac{4+\sqrt6}{6-\sqrt6}
=\frac{3+\sqrt6}{3}.
\]

Let

\[
R_1=3,\qquad 
R_2=\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3},\qquad 
R_3=\frac{3+\sqrt6}{3}.
\]

Then

\[
R_1R_2R_3=1,
\]

and

\[
R_1>R_3>1>R_2>0.
\]

For a given solution, suppose \(R(u)=R_i\) and \(R(v)=R_j\), with the remaining index \(k\). Then

\[
y=xR_i,\qquad z=xR_iR_j,
\]

so

\[
xyz=x^3R_i^2R_j=3.
\]

Because \(R_1R_2R_3=1\),

\[
R_i^2R_j=\frac{R_i}{R_k}.
\]

Thus

\[
x^3=\frac{3}{R_i^2R_j}=\frac{3R_k}{R_i}.
\]

To minimize \(x\), we minimize \(x^3\), so we take the smallest possible ratio \(R_k/R_i\). This occurs when \(k=2\) and \(i=1\), giving

\[
x_{\min}^3=3\cdot\frac{R_2}{R_1}=3\cdot\frac{\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}}{3}
=\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}.
\]

Therefore

\[
x_{\min}=\sqrt[3]{\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}}.
\]

This value is attainable, for example with

\[
x=\sqrt[3]{\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}},\qquad
y=3x,\qquad
z=(3+\sqrt6)x.
\]

Hence the minimum possible value of \(x\) is

\[
\boxed{\sqrt[3]{\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}}}
\]
